remaining_gaps: ending_or_current_basis: no clause end can be dated. Every clause concerns the Commission, and sec. 4(b) (49 FR 61634: 'The Commission shall terminate thirty days after submitting its report') makes the Commission's end the date the report was actually submitted plus 30 days. The held sources give only deadlines: sec. 2(b) (December 31, 1982), as amended by EO 12397 (January 15, 1983) and EO 12402 (January 20, 1983). A report deadline is not the date of submission. The reporting command in sec. 2(b) is also a one-time command that was spent when the report was submitted, so EO 12534 sec. 3(e) (effective 1985-09-30; it revokes the order as one of the committees that 'have terminated') is only an upper bound, not a first end (the EO 13792 rejection lesson). Needed: an official record of the date the Commission's report was transmitted to the President (Weekly Compilation / Public Papers of the Presidents 1983, or the report itself).

ending_or_current_basis: no clause end can be dated. Sec. 4(b), as amended by EO 12442 sec. 2 (signed 1983-09-21), says the Commission 'shall, unless sooner extended, terminate 30 days after it transmits its final report to the President'; sec. 2(d) as amended by EO 12442 sec. 1 only sets a deadline (November 30, 1984). The held sources do not record the date the final report was actually transmitted, and a deadline is not that date. The lapse check under original sec. 4(b) (60 days after the final report or December 31, 1983, whichever earlier) is closed from the held texts: EO 12442 replaced sec. 4(b) on 1983-09-21, before December 31, 1983 and before any final report was due under the order. EO 12534 sec. 3(n) (effective 1985-09-30) is a cleanup revocation of a body it describes as already terminated, so it is only an upper bound. Needed: an official record of the final report's transmittal date (Public Papers of the Presidents 1984, or the report 'Report to the President by the President's Commission on Indian Reservation Economies').

ending_or_current_basis: no clause end can be dated. Sec. 4(b) says the Commission 'shall, unless otherwise extended, terminate 60 days after submitting its final report'; the report deadline was December 1, 1983 (sec. 2(b)), moved to February 1, 1984 by EO 12449. The held sources do not record the date the final report was submitted, and a deadline is not that date. The Commission's reporting command was a one-time command spent on submission, so EO 12534 sec. 3(d) (effective 1985-09-30, a cleanup revocation of a body described as already terminated) is only an upper bound. Needed: an official record of the final report's submission date (Public Papers of the Presidents 1984 or the report itself); the first end of the Commission clauses is that date plus 60 days.

ending_or_current_basis: no clause end can be dated. Sec. 4(b) says the Task Force 'shall, unless sooner extended, terminate thirty days after submission of its report to the President, but in no event later than January 31, 1984'. The end is the earlier of (report date + 30 days) and January 31, 1984; sec. 2 only required the report within ninety days of the first meeting, and neither the first meeting date nor the report date is held. The outer limit is an upper bound, not a first end: it equals the first end only if the report was submitted after January 1, 1984. EO 12534 sec. 3(l) (effective 1985-09-30) is a cleanup revocation of a body it describes as already terminated, so it cannot supply the end. Needed: an official record of the report's submission date (Weekly Compilation / Public Papers of the Presidents 1983-84, or the Task Force report).

ending_or_current_basis: first end not established. Sec. 4(b) fixes the Task Group's end at September 30, 1985 'unless its existence is sooner extended in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act', and EO 12534 sec. 3(i) revokes the order the same day, but Pub. If that statute ended the Task Group on reporting, the first end of the Task Group clauses is earlier than 1985-09-30. Needed: the text and effective date of sec. 1632 of Pub. ending_or_current_basis: sec. 2(b) ('shall report ... not later than July 15, 1985') is a one-time reporting command that was spent when the report was submitted, which may be earlier than the order's own term. The date the report was actually submitted is not held, so whether clause 2(b) ends with the Task Group (September 30, 1985) or on submission cannot be settled; a deadline is not a completion date and the EO 12534 revocation is only an upper bound.

ending_or_current_basis: no clause end can be dated. Sec. 4(b) ends the Commission at the earlier of 30 days after submission of its report and September 30, 1985; the order requires three sequential reports (February 15, March 1 and March 15, 1985), so even the meaning of 'its report' (final or each) and the actual submission dates are not held, and deadlines are not submission dates. September 30, 1985 is only an upper bound: EO 12534 sec. 3(a) (effective the same day) is a cleanup revocation of a body it describes as already terminated. Needed: an official record of the date the Commission's final report was transmitted to the President (Public Papers of the Presidents 1985, or the report itself).

ending_or_current_basis: Pub. L. 98-525 sec. 1511 (98 Stat. 2492 ff.), under which the Commission was established, is not held; read it for any statutory term of the Commission earlier than September 30, 1985, and for the reports it requires.

ending_or_current_basis: first end not established for any of the three clauses. EO 12496 (50 FR 211) sec. 6 states only that 'Executive Order No. 12456 of December 30, 1983, as amended, is superseded', with no effective-date wording of its own; sec. 5 gives the new Schedule 7 judicial salary rates effect 'on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1985', which is a pay-period rule, not a calendar date. No held source fixes the pay period that applied to judicial salaries in January 1985, and whether the supersession of Schedule 8 took effect on signing (the held text prints the heading date as December 26 and the signature date as December 28, 1984) or with the new rates is not settled by the acting text. A superseded rate schedule is a standing command, so its end is the effective date of the replacing rates, but that date cannot be computed from held sources. Needed: the judicial-salary pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1985 (Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts or OPM pay-period calendar 1985) and a page-image check of the EO 12496 heading and signature date.
